reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about the predictive power of ML with disorder descriptors and the limitations of conventional models, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these key premises. All claims are presented without reference to earlier experimental or computational results.
premises: ML with atomic-scale disorder descriptors can capture complex phonon scattering in HEAs
Conventional models (rule-of-mixtures, mean-field) fail to capture disorder effects on thermal conductivity
Disorder-sensitive descriptors (local chemical environments, mixing enthalpy, SRO) strongly influence phonon scattering
The approach will yield ≥20% higher prediction accuracy than conventional models
Applicability is limited to HEAs without extreme compositions or phase separation/ordering
